stem:
The compound Advantame is a sweetener that tastes approximately 25000 times sweeter than sucrose.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Advantame is optically active.

On the diagram of Advantame, circle all the chiral carbon atoms.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The decomposition of Advantame produces three molecules, $\mathbf{J}$, $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{L}$. The $\text{RO}-$ group in Advantame is unreactive.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}
parts.text: Suggest possible reagents and conditions for this decomposition.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction occurring.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Draw the structure of $\mathbf{L}$ in the box above.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Aqueous bromine was added dropwise to a solution of $\mathbf{J}$ until the bromine was in excess.

State what you would observe.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{J}$ has the molecular formula $\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{19}\text{O}_{6}\text{N}$.

Use this formula to write an equation for the reaction of excess aqueous sodium hydroxide with **one** mole of $\mathbf{J}$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: State what you would observe when an excess of aqueous bromine is added to a solution of $\mathbf{K}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{K}$ can be polymerised.

Draw the structure of the polymer showing **two** repeat units. The linkage between the monomer units should be fully displayed.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: State how many different carbon environments are present in $\mathbf{K}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
The chemical shifts, $\delta$, due to two of the carbon atoms x and y present in $\mathbf{K}$ are given in the table.

| carbon atom | $\delta / \text{ppm}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| x | 130 |
| y | 170 |

On the structure of $\mathbf{K}$, circle **and** label **two** carbon atoms which could correspond to x and y.
